Everything starts here. Session 1 opens with a real case study — a string of bank robberies cracked by a statistical model you won't be able to read yet, and that's deliberate: by Session 12 you'll build that exact model yourself. Tonight covers the map (how the course works), the raw material (types of data and levels of measurement), and your first R commands. The swirl homework then keeps your hands moving in R all week, because starting with Session 2 our running example turns real: 30,000 crimes reported in Chicago in 2025.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this week you can:

- name the four levels of measurement and classify any variable into them
- explain why a variable's level of measurement constrains the math *and* the plots you may use
- run your first R commands in RStudio, and know what to install before Session 2
- find your way around this site, the syllabus, and the weekly rhythm of the course

## Before class

- Install R and RStudio — [step-by-step guide](../resources.qmd#installing-r-and-rstudio)
- Read: Stanton **Introduction** and **Appendices A–C**
- Read: this site's [Syllabus](../syllabus.qmd)

## In class

- Course tour: syllabus, this website, how the semester works
- Why statistics is awesome (with real crime-data examples)
- Types of data and levels of measurement
- Guided tour of R and RStudio

*Missed class? The [demo walkthrough](../demos/demo-01-intro.qmd) reproduces today's live demos step by step.*

## Homework

**swirl tutorials** — interactive R lessons that run inside R itself:

```r
install.packages("swirl")
library(swirl)
swirl()
```

When prompted, choose the **R Programming** course and complete these lessons:

1. Basic Building Blocks
2. Workspace and Files
3. Sequences of Numbers
4. Vectors
5. Missing Values
6. Subsetting Vectors
7. Matrices and Data Frames
8. Logic
12. Looking at Data
15. Base Graphics

Save the R script you work in as you go (one script per lesson is fine). Submit your R script files via Canvas **by 11:59 pm Sunday** ahead of Session 2.

### Before Session 2

- Read Stanton **Ch. 1** *(and if you couldn't finish the Intro and Appendices A–C before the first class, complete them this week)*
- Read R4DS **[Ch. 1 — Data visualization](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-visualize.html)** and **[Ch. 2 — Workflow: basics](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-basics.html)**
- **R4DS exercises** — not all of them, just these five:
  - **1.2.5** #3 (build a scatterplot) and **#5** (the code is broken — find and fix it)
  - **1.4.3** #4 (same histogram, different `binwidth` — which one tells the truth?)
  - **1.5.5** #2 (add a *third* variable to a scatterplot three different ways)
  - **2.5** #2 (three lines, three errors — this is the exercise that teaches you to read R's error messages)

**These are required and submitted.** Ch. 1 uses the `palmerpenguins` data, so install it once first:

```r
install.packages(c("palmerpenguins", "ggthemes"))
```

Put your answers in an `.R` script — one clearly labelled block per exercise number — and submit it via Canvas alongside your swirl scripts, **by 11:59 pm Sunday**.
